bug_description.normalized: The staged OpenType font reaches HarfBuzz's CFF1 CID font-dict parser in `OT::cff1::accelerator_templ_t::init`. The attacker-controlled `fdArray->count` exceeds the outer `hb_vector_t<CFF1FontDictValues>` inline capacity of 8, so the ninth `fontDicts.push()` migrates the first eight parsed font-dict objects from `static_array[8]` to heap. That migration uses raw `memcpy`, which shallow-copies each `CFF1FontDictValues` object, including any already-allocated nested `hb_vector_t<OpStr>::arrayZ_` pointers, while leaving the original inline owners live. A later `fini(); return;` cleanup path inside the same `init` deep-frees the heap copy through `fontDicts.fini_deep()`. When the accelerator object itself is later destroyed, C++ still destructs the stale inline `static_array` elements, and their copied `hb_vector_t<OpStr>` members free the same buffer again, producing the ASan heap double-free. The staged patch changes only the default `hb_vector_t` inline capacity from 8 to 2 in `src/hb-vector.hh`; no fixed-version execution is staged here, so the GT records that diff without treating it as witnessed crash suppression.

source.description: First vulnerability-relevant project read of attacker-controlled CFF state. `init()` has already accepted the CID `FDArray` and now materializes its count as the loop bound that drives how many `CFF1FontDictValues` objects will be pushed into `fontDicts`.
source.value_from: The fuzzed OpenType font's CFF1 `FDArray` inside the blob referenced by `face`; after `fdArray` and `fdSelect` pass structural sanitization, `fdArray->count` becomes `fdCount` and controls the later `for (i < fdCount)` parse loop.
source.note: The saved crash necessarily takes the CID-only path, because non-CID fonts never enter the `FDArray` / `fontDicts` loop that triggers the vulnerable inline-to-heap copy.

sink.description: ASan crash site. A stale inline copy of a `CFF1FontDictValues` object's nested `hb_vector_t<OpStr>` reaches `fini()` during accelerator destruction and frees `arrayZ_` even though the same heap buffer was already freed from the heap copy during earlier cleanup.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports the second free at `src/hb-vector.hh:63:7` in `hb_vector_t<CFF::OpStr, 8u>::fini()`.

root_cause.description: Unsafe ownership duplication. When `fontDicts` grows out of inline storage, `alloc()` copies the existing inline `CFF1FontDictValues` objects byte-for-byte from `static_array` into a heap buffer. For these non-trivial objects that already own nested `hb_vector_t<OpStr>` allocations, the raw `memcpy` duplicates the inner `arrayZ_` pointers without destroying or clearing the original inline owners.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes `template <typename Type, unsigned int PreallocedCount=8>` to `...=2` in `src/hb-vector.hh`, which alters when this inline-to-heap copy path is entered. Stage 02 has only vulnerable-version evidence, so the GT records that observable diff but does not treat it as fixed-runtime proof for this witness.

parser_admitted.description: The fuzzed font has passed earlier CFF1 table/header checks and entered the CID-specific font-dict parsing path; only this branch populates `fontDicts` from `FDArray`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled `fdCount` loop bound that forces the outer `fontDicts` vector past its inline capacity and into the vulnerable copy path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the staged `poc` bytes in an `hb_face_t` and the first `trySubset()` call at line 64 invokes `hb_subset()` on the fixed ASCII codepoint set. The saved crash happens on this first subset attempt, not on the later text-from-data path.
Subsetting starts by creating a subset plan, which immediately computes the glyph set to retain before any table rewriting.
The plan builder constructs a local CFF1 accelerator and initializes it from the fuzzed face at line 109; this CFF initialization is where the double-free chain is set up.

CID `FDArray` parsing pushes multiple `CFF1FontDictValues` into `fontDicts`, allocates nested `OpStr` vectors while interpreting those dicts, and later enters a `fini(); return;` cleanup path inside `init`.

The outer vector's inline-to-heap migration copies owning font-dict objects with `memcpy`, duplicating nested `OpStr` pointers; cleanup frees the heap copy first, and later destruction of the stale inline copy frees the same `OpStr` buffer again.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the CID path, `init()` resolves the attacker-controlled `FDArray` / `FDSelect` from the CFF blob, accepts them after sanitization, and reads `fdCount` from the font. That count becomes the bound for the later `fontDicts` push loop.

fine_trace.code: for (unsigned int i = 0; i < fdCount; i++)
fine_trace.note: The CID font-dict parser iterates once per attacker-controlled `FDArray` entry. The later outer-vector reallocation proves this witness reaches at least a ninth iteration, i.e. `fdCount` exceeds the vulnerable inline capacity of 8.

Each iteration materializes one `CFF1FontDictValues` object in `fontDicts`. For the first eight iterations on the vulnerable build, `fontDicts.arrayZ_` is still null and `push()` therefore returns slots from `fontDicts.static_array[8]`, so these parsed font-dict objects live inline inside the accelerator object.

While `font_interp.interpret(*font)` parses one of those inline font dicts, `add_op()` grows its nested `values` vector. ASan's allocation stack names this `add_op` -> `hb_vector_t<CFF::OpStr>::push/alloc` chain as the origin of the 912-byte `OpStr` buffer that is later double-freed, so by the time step 6 runs at least one inline `fontDicts.static_array[i]` owns a non-null `values.arrayZ_` heap buffer.

On the ninth outer `fontDicts.push()`, `size` has advanced to 9 while `allocated` is still the inline capacity 8. This fast-path guard is therefore false, so `fontDicts` leaves inline storage and enters the copy branch in `alloc()`.

Root cause. Because the growth happens while `fontDicts` still uses inline storage, `alloc()` heap-allocates `new_array` and byte-copies the first `len` inline `CFF1FontDictValues` objects out of `static_array`. That shallow copy duplicates each copied object's nested `values.arrayZ_` pointer into the heap array, but the original inline owners remain alive in `static_array`.

ASan's previous-free stack shows that one of `init()`'s later `{ fini(); return; }` cleanup sites executes after step 6. `fontDicts.fini_deep()` walks the heap copy in `arrayZ_` and frees each copied `CFF1FontDictValues`' nested `values.arrayZ_` buffer once. The stale inline copies created in step 6 are not destroyed or cleared here; they remain in `fontDicts.static_array`.

Sink. After `_populate_gids_to_retain` unwinds, destruction of the still-live `fontDicts.static_array[...]` elements auto-destroys their copied `hb_vector_t<OpStr>` members. Those inline copies still hold the same `arrayZ_` pointer that step 7 already freed from the heap copy, so this second `free(arrayZ_)` triggers the ASan double-free.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is the one-line `hb_vector_t` default `PreallocedCount` change (`8 -> 2`) in `src/hb-vector.hh`. No fixed image or fixed-version execution is staged here, so the GT does not treat that diff alone as demonstrated resolution of the saved double-free witness.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is an OpenType font. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` wraps it in an `hb_face_t`, and the first `trySubset()` call at line 64 invokes `hb_subset()` on the fixed ASCII codepoint set. Inside `OT::cff1::accelerator_templ_t::init`, the font takes the CID Font DICT path with `fdCount > 8`; at least one of the first eight inline `CFF1FontDictValues` acquires a heap-backed nested `values.arrayZ_` before the ninth push, the outer vector then `memcpy`-copies those inline owners to heap, and a later init cleanup path plus final accelerator destruction free that same nested `OpStr` buffer twice.

format.name: OpenType font data with a CID-keyed CFF1 table
format.contract: An OpenType font whose CFF1 `FDArray` count exceeds 8, where at least one of the first eight parsed `CFF1FontDictValues` grows its nested `hb_vector_t<OpStr>` onto the heap before the ninth `fontDicts.push()`, and where a later `fini(); return;` cleanup path inside `accelerator_templ_t::init` is taken.
